raw_response:
I will start from what worked for me these past few years and adjust for scale, water, and price. With 220.1 mu, I cannot manage this like a tiny household plot. I need a plan that is steady, easy to execute, and not too risky. In Quzhou, water is a real advantage when the rain turns uneven, so I will use that to protect emergence and grain filling instead of gambling on the sky. For millet, I will not push nitrogen too hard, because too much vegetative growth can make management messy and does not always turn into grain. I will keep phosphorus and potassium in the base fertilizer so the stand is stronger and the ears fill better. For soybean, I will keep nitrogen lower and give more attention to phosphorus and potassium, because if I feed soybean too much nitrogen, I spend extra money and the crop gets lazy. Since I have only farmed 5 years, I will stay with improved seed rather than gamble on weak local seed. I will also keep pesticide passes limited but timely, because on a large area like mine, one missed outbreak costs more than one spray. I grow both crops, so this year I will split the land 120 mu to millet and 100.1 mu to soybean. That gives me a workable labor schedule, spreads risk, and fits what I can manage with irrigation and machinery.
